definition: Formula-level expression for the arising side of sakkāya understood through the five clung-to heaps.
notes: Use this phrase when the text explicitly treats appropriated identity dynamically. The formula inherits the technical sakkāya default identity and should not be flattened into self-language. The personal identity alternate is allowed only when explanatory prose needs the fuller phrase.

context_rules.context: In direct doctrinal translation of the formula
In explanatory prose where a fuller phrase is needed
context_rules.notes: Use this in explanatory prose only for clarification.

example_phrases.notes: Shows the formula line tied to the five clung-to heaps by the governing sakkāya entry.

translation_policy.default_scope: Use this as the standard wording for the arising side of the governed sakkāya arising-and-quenching pair, where identity is treated through the five clung-to heaps.
translation_policy.when_not_to_apply: Do not use this wording where samudaya governs a subject other than appropriated identity, and do not rewrite the line as the arising of a self.
translation_policy.drift_risk: Prevents samudaya from drifting toward creation-language and sakkāya from drifting into self-language, which together would present identity as a thing that comes into being rather than a process that is put together.
